title: Execution of a template sequence
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, and let $tau$ be a list of $n$ micro-operations, each printing a bit or printing a register in unary. Let $lab:mathbb{N}\toLambda$ be labels and let $nu\inLambda$. Suppose that at every index $i\le n$, the instruction at $lab(i)$ is the instruction prescribed by the template at $i$: it performs the corresponding micro-operation and goes to $lab(i+1)$ when $i<n$, and goes to $nu$ when $i=n$. Then, for every register assignment $rho$ and input position $p$, from label $lab(0)$ the program reaches $nu$ within $n+1$ steps, with the register assignment and input position unchanged and with the template’s concatenated output appended to the existing output.

replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, let
$\tau = (m_0, \dots, m_{n-1})$ be a list of micro-operations, each either
``print a bit $b$'' or ``print register $r$ in unary'', and let
$\lambda : \mathbb{N} \to \Lambda$ and $\nu \in \Lambda$ be labels.  Suppose that
for each $i < n$ the instruction of $P$ at $\lambda(i)$ performs $m_i$ and then
goes to $\lambda(i+1)$, and the instruction at $\lambda(n)$ is
$\mathsf{goto}\ \nu$.  Then for all registers $\rho$ and input positions $p$,
from label $\lambda(0)$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read the program
reaches label $\nu$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read within $n + 1$
steps, appending $w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ to its output, where $w_i$ is $b$ if
$m_i$ prints the bit $b$ and $w_i = 1^{\rho(r)}$ if $m_i$ prints register $r$.
